title: tenant-prefetch-router-econ-optimizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a tenant-aware prefetch router and econ optimizer behind a feature flag; CLI dry-run mode for deterministic simulation; safe canary rollout and rollback on regressions.
description: Context: customers operate mixed workloads and tuning batching/caching/quant defaults is manual and error-prone. This PR introduces a tenant-prefetch router that consumes tenant signals and schedules warmup/prefill windows with soft constraints and safety fallbacks, plus an econ-driven optimizer that synthesizes candidate profiles (batch size, prefill window, cache retention, quant profile) and scores them with a cost-latency utility. Changes: 1) router: new server-side routing component that queues prefill jobs, enforces tenant isolation heuristics, and exposes an opt-in apply API; 2) optimizer: offline simulation path and an online conservative mode that proposes changes and can auto-apply with rollback triggers; 3) telemetry: new histograms and spans (prefill.success_rate, econ.recommendation_score, tenant.warmstart_latency_p95) for debugging and policy evaluation; 4) CLI: prefetchctl dry-run to run deterministic simulations against archived traces; 5) policy: feature-flag gating, canary targeting, and an auto-apply guard that reverts changes on unit-econ regressions or latency SLO violations. Motivation: cut per-tenant unit cost while meeting latency SLOs and reduce ops burden for Dedicated/Private customers. Rollout: staged canary in Dedicated pool A -> Dedicated pool B -> hosted shadow-only; default off for existing customers. Compatibility: backward-compatible; router only changes live behavior after a profile apply. Metrics to watch: latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, prefill hit ratio, coldstart rate, quantized-fallback rate. Related subsystems: workload-profiling, prefill-scheduler, telemetry and cost-synthesizer.
